newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to tap CDC for two of 10-bln-franc savings.
newsitem.headline: France to tap CDC for two of 10-bln-franc savings.

text.p: A French finance ministry official said on Thursday two of the 10 billion francs in planned savings to trim the 1997 public deficit would come from state bank Caisse des Depots, on top of two billion in defence cuts.
No decision had been taken on the precise source of the other six billion of savings, which would come from the civil budget, or other public sector reserves, the official said.

Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn announced the plans for 10 billion francs of savings as part of a 32 billion franc package that also includes 22 billion francs from corporate tax increases to nudge France's public deficit down towards three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year.

"The only decision that has been taken is to use two billion francs from the Caisse des Depots (CDC) with the full agreement of its board and managing director," said the official, noting that it had already been announced that two billion would come from the defence budget.
"For the remainder, the government will actively pursue its search for savings in the civil budget and the treasury of public establishments," said the official.
The official said various media reports had been speculating on the public sector company sources for the remainder of the 10 billion in savings.

The total 32 billion franc package was unveiled on Monday at the same time as an audit commissioned by the Socialist-led government estimated that France's public deficit this year was heading for 3.5 to 3.7 percent of GDP.
The government said the package would knock 0.4 percentage points off the 1997 deficit figure.

The Maastricht treaty sets a deficit goal of three percent of GDP in 1997 to qualify for European monetary union, but does not stipulate 3.0 percent and the French government has said it does not want a dogmatic reading of the treaty as meaning 3.0 percent.

Strauss-Kahn also said on Monday that France's 1998 budget would be drawn up on the basis of bringing the public deficit to three percent of GDP next year, a goal reaffirmed by government sources on Thursday.
He has also said France's deficit could come in at three percent in 1997 if the economy picked up more vigorously as the year progressed.
